title: Decoding Regeneration: Transcriptomic Profiling of the Early Genetic Response to Injury in the Annelid, Lumbriculus variegatus
content: Full-body regeneration remains one of biology's most unexplored processes. The freshwater annelid Lumbriculus variegatus is a model system known for its exceptional regenerative capabilities. A high-quality de novotranscriptome was assembled from regenerating segments, and transcriptomic profiling of early regeneration (0 h, 2 h, 4 h post-amputation) was performed to identify the initial molecular signature of stem cell activation. The assembly comprised 250,866 contigs (96.5% BUSCO score) and 279,334 predicted proteins, with 8,796 confidently identified protein-coding genes. Within 2 hours, 452 genes were differentially expressed, with predominant downregulation (429 genes, 94.9%). Among 23 upregulated genes, 17 were newly activated from complete transcriptional silence, with fold-changes ranging from 6.4- to 512-fold. By 4 hours, the response shifted toward activation, with 83 genes upregulated versus only 1 downregulated. Temporal analysis revealed three distinct expression patterns: increasing, stable, and decreasing. Functional annotation assigned putative functions to candidates including ISL-1 (a LIM/homeodomain transcription factor linked to neuron differentiation), TRIM proteins (ubiquitination), lectins, kinases, ATM kinase, and Fanconi anemia protein. Notably, several genes overlap with regeneration-associated genes identified in other annelids, including stem cell regulators (piwi/vasa) and MAPK signaling components. The top two candidates lacked BLAST homologs but received KEGG KO assignments and DeepProGo predictions, representing genes potentially specific to L. variegatus and novel regulators of spiralian regeneration. These findings reveal both conserved regeneration principles and potential spiralian innovations, establishing this organism as a powerful model for regenerative biology.
